newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog markets early Wednesday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher than Tuesday's top prices, sand building strength amid aggressive packer demand and lighter marketings, dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $51.00 to $52.50 at plants. However, at least one central Iowa packer buyer said he expected prices to be higher before the day is over.
Illinois hog prices were up $0.50 early and seen up $1.00 by the end of the day, dealers there said. Illinois hogs sold $50.50-$51.50 in the country and $52.00-$52.50 at plants.

Indiana buyers said hogs were trading at steady prices at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $50.00-$51.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold were steady and trading at $49.00 to $50.00 in the country and $50.00 to $51.00 at plants.
Marketings reportedly were slowing down from big numbers early this week as producers start working through the hogs that were backed up by last week's winter storm, they said.

Cash hog prices also were seen rebounding amid strong demand from packers with profitable operating margins, sources said. Strength also was attributed to ideas that declines in pork prices was starting to attract renewed retail buying.
